discovered-from:LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V

The slot_schedule removal (LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V) removes the time-based slot schedule from proxy/config.yaml, config-fast.yaml, config-cheap.yaml.

The proxy-usage-analysis skill (.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/) still parses slot_schedule from the active config to derive per-time slot counts and ctx: scripts/config_loader.py (_normalize), scripts/bucketing.py (schedule_from_config), scripts/reporting.py (ctx_by_time), scripts/recommendations.py (advice pointing at 'proxy/config.yaml slot_schedule').

Impact: with no slot_schedule key, config_loader omits it and bucketing falls back to a single 'fast' bucket with default_slots (session_slot_pool_size) for the whole day — the cheap (2-slot) vs fast (3-slot) slot-count split is lost.

Required work (in the skill directory, per .pi boundary this item must be explicitly authorized):
- Derive per-mode slot counts from the mode profiles' static session_slot_pool_size (fast 3 / cheap 2) instead of schedule entries.
- Replace ctx_by_time semantics with the profiles' static local_model_ctx_size.
- Update recommendations text that references 'proxy/config.yaml slot_schedule'.
- Update skill tests/fixtures accordingly.

# Give the model (fallback chain) config control over the free-tier request budget

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want to set the free-tier request-budget behaviour
**per model / fallback chain** (with sensible global defaults), so I can tune
`plan`, `author`, `code` and `compact` independently — instead of every model
inheriting one global setting — while any single provider entry can still
override its own behaviour.

## Current state

- `rate_limit_rpm` is a **provider-entry** field (`provider_cfg`), so it is
  already configurable per entry — today only `munitoai-free` sets it (10).
- The four *behaviour* knobs are read **server-wide only**:
  `server.provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_waiters`,
  `server.provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py::_config_value`, called with the server
  config).
- `acquire_provider_budget(provider_cfg, config, session_id, request)` is **not**
  given `model_config`/the model name, so a model-scoped setting cannot be
  expressed today — a single reserve ratio / wait cap applies to all chains.
- `affinity_ttl_seconds` is applied in three places, all of which read the same
  server config today: `acquire_provider_budget()`,
  `record_provider_affinity()` (via `provider.py::_maybe_record_provider_affinity`)
  and `provider_affinity_active()`. Honouring a model-scoped TTL (AC1) therefore
  requires threading the model config into the affinity record/lookup path too,
  not only into the acquire call.
- Both budget call sites in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` are
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (~line 7128) and
  `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (~line 8141); each already holds the request's
  `model_config`.
- Consequence: an interactive chain (e.g. `plan`) and a background chain (e.g.
  `compact`) cannot trade latency against free-tier utilisation differently, and
  a future gated entry cannot be tuned without changing global behaviour.
- Caveat on `compact`: `models.compact` is consumed only by
  `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`, which dispatches to its providers
  directly over httpx and never calls the gate. A `models.compact.budget` block
  is therefore accepted and resolvable but has **no runtime effect** until that
  dispatch is gated (tracked separately — see OPEN QUESTION 1).

## Desired change

Add a **model-level `budget` block** with precedence
**provider entry > model block > server default > built-in default**:

```yaml
models:
  plan:
    budget:
      reserve_ratio: 0.4        # share of rate_limit_rpm reserved for in-progress
      wait_max_seconds: 10      # per-request wait cap for in-progress sessions
      max_waiters: 4            # concurrent waiter cap
      affinity_ttl_seconds: 600 # how long a session counts as in-progress
    providers:
      - name: munitoai-free
        rate_limit_rpm: 15      # entry-level override of the budget size
        budget:                 # optional per-entry behaviour override
          reserve_ratio: 0.2
```

- All five keys are optional at every layer; absent keys fall through to the next
  layer, so **existing configs behave exactly as today**.
- Values are clamped/validated exactly as the server-level knobs are today
  (ratio to `[0,1]`, wait/TTL to `>= 0`, malformed values fall back to the
  default with a warning — fail open, never fail closed).
- The effective values are visible per request in the budget logs/attempt
  diagnostics (which layer supplied `reserve_slots`/`effective_limit`), and the
  provider diagnostics table keeps showing remaining/limit per entry.
- The budget **bucket** remains keyed by provider entry (one account quota shared
  by `plan`/`author`/`code` even when their model blocks differ) — document this
  explicitly so per-model tuning is not mistaken for per-model quota.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `models.<name>.budget` block is honoured for `reserve_ratio`,
   `wait_max_seconds`, `max_waiters` and `affinity_ttl_seconds`, and a provider
   entry may override any of them with its own `budget` block.
2. Precedence is exactly entry > model > server > built-in default, proven by
   tests for every key (single-layer and multi-layer combinations).
3. Omitting all blocks reproduces today's behaviour byte-for-byte — identical
   `BudgetDecision` values (`reserve_slots`, `effective_limit`, `reason`) and
   identical log lines for the shipped `config.yaml` (no behavioural change;
   tested).
4. Malformed/out-of-range values fall back to the next layer with a logged
   warning and never raise or block a request (tests for each key).
5. The budget bucket stays shared per provider entry across models; a test proves
   two models with different `budget` blocks still consume one `rate_limit_rpm`
   window.
6. The effective configuration is visible in the budget skip/wait log lines and
   the attempt diagnostics (source layer included), and the provider diagnostics
   table keeps showing remaining/limit.
7. Tests cover both real fallback entry points —
   `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` —
   proving each passes the request's model config into the gate. (The intake's
   third clause, "the compaction/summarizer path where it reaches the same
   gate", is **not implementable as written**: `models.compact` is consumed only
   by `build_compact_summarizer()`, which calls providers directly over httpx
   and never reaches the gate. See OPEN QUESTION 1 and the follow-up item.)
8. Documentation updated: `proxy/config.yaml` header comments + a commented
   example, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
   (model-level `budget` block alongside the `providers` list).
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Config-shape only: no change to gate semantics, reserve maths, or the
  affinity/wait design.
- Keep every layer optional; no migration of existing configs required.
- Do not introduce per-model *quota* (a separate budget per model) — that would
  break the one-account-per-entry model; if it is ever wanted, it must be a
  separate decision.
- The gate must remain fail-open when the new blocks are absent or malformed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — resolve each knob through the new
  entry > model > server precedence; extend `BudgetDecision`/logs with the source
  layer.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — pass `model_config` (and the model key) into
  `acquire_provider_budget()` from both fallback entry points
  (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`) and into
  `_maybe_record_provider_affinity()` so the recorded TTL matches the model.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` — precedence/validation/shared-bucket
  tests, plus the call-site wiring test (the module already imports
  `proxy.provider as provider`, so no new test module is needed).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — document the `models.<name>.budget` block; commented
  example.
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` + fixtures — only if the new keys are
  introduced as shipped values (they are optional; likely no fixture change).
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — docs.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Add failing tests in `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` for precedence,
   validation/fallback and the shared-bucket guarantee (AC1–AC5).
2. Implement the layered resolver in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
   (entry > model > server > built-in) and extend `BudgetDecision`/log lines
   with the source layer (AC6).
3. Thread `model_config` through both `provider.py` call sites and the affinity
   record/lookup path (AC1 `affinity_ttl_seconds`, AC7).
4. Update docs: `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/README.md`,
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (AC8).
5. Run the suite via the test skill (AC9).

## OPEN QUESTIONS

1. **Compaction/summarizer path and the budget gate.** AC7 originally asked for
   coverage of "the compaction/summarizer path where it reaches the same gate".
   Fact check (this session): `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`
   (`build_compact_summarizer` / `_remote_chat_url`) resolves
   `models.compact.providers` itself and calls each provider **directly over
   httpx**, bypassing `localhost:8080` — so it never reaches
   `acquire_provider_budget()` and no `budget` block applies to it.
   AC7 was therefore narrowed to the two real fallback entry points and the gap
   was filed as `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` (Gate the models.compact summarizer
   dispatch through the provider budget).
   **Preferred option (a): accept the split** — it preserves the "config-shape
   only" constraint and leaves eight of nine ACs unblocked; the summarizer gate
   is tracked separately. Alternative (b): widen this item to gate the
   summarizer dispatch as well (larger effort, and the `compact` half of the
   user story only becomes real then). Producer decision requested — see the
   comment on this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is `rate_limit_rpm` used for any other provider (would per-model tuning
  matter beyond the free tier)?" Answer (Map, 2026-10-18, comment
  `LP-C0MVDVL1IR002EH5X`): no — `munitoai-free` is the only entry declaring it;
  the capability is dormant for every other provider, and the bucket is keyed by
  provider entry so `plan`/`author`/`code` share one 10/min window.
- Q: "Do both `provider.py` budget call sites have `model_config` available, and
  what are the functions called?" Answer (this session, code inspection): yes —
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (~line 7128) and
  `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (~line 8145); the AC7 name `_proxy_with_fallback`
  was corrected accordingly.
- OPEN QUESTION 1 (compaction/summarizer gate) — see above; needs a producer
  decision before the item is implemented. It does not block the other eight
  ACs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — reserve + 15 s wait cap (introduced the knobs this item
  makes per-model).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` — the original budget gate.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — evaluating whether the `munitoai-free` budget itself
  should be raised (the first consumer of per-model tuning).
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — restricting the free tier to cheap mode (another
  model-scoped policy that could share this configuration shape).
- `LP-0MVDUZ0E10011W3C` (in progress) — rewrites the limiter/budget skip log
  lines that AC6 extends; sequence with it so the two log changes do not
  conflict.
- `LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY` (open) — consolidating the fallback-chain configuration
  docs, of which the `budget` block docs (AC8) are one part.
- `LP-0MVF2DNCX003Z5CO` (in progress) — per-model context size, an existing
  example of a model-level knob read per request.
- Follow-up (filed this session) — `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` — gate the
  `models.compact` summarizer dispatch so a `budget` block has runtime effect
  there.
data.title: Give the model/fallback-chain config control over free-tier budget knobs

# Automated tests: per-model token aggregation in /logs UI

## Summary

Playwright UI test for the per-model token summary section added to the `/logs` page summary header. Loads the page with an injected `window.__INITIAL_STATS` snapshot containing model-suffixed token-count keys (both `-> model:<name>` and bare `model:<name>` patterns, plus keys with no model suffix) and asserts the per-model aggregation renders correctly.

## Problem Statement

The per-model token summary (LP-0MVE592AU008VAP4) adds client-side aggregation logic to `renderSummary()` in `view_logs.html`. That logic must be verified automatically: correct per-model grouping, correct sent/recv and category totals, unknown-model fallback, and no regression of the existing per-endpoint display.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Playwright spec exists under `proxy/tests/` that loads the `/logs` page with an injected `window.__INITIAL_STATS` snapshot containing keys with `-> model:<name>` suffixes, bare `model:<name>` keys, and keys without any model suffix (e.g. `-> local`).
- The spec asserts one summary row per distinct model with correct total sent and total recv values.
- The spec asserts the per-model category breakdown (User / Assistant / Tool / System sent; Response recv) matches the fixture values.
- The spec asserts keys without a model suffix are grouped under an "unknown" model row rather than dropped.
- The spec asserts the existing per-endpoint token section still renders its correct values (no double-counting or breakage regression).
- The spec passes under the Playwright runner against the local proxy.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/model-tokens.spec.js` — new Playwright spec
- `proxy/tests/slot-logs.spec.js` — pattern reference for fake SSE / injected stats
- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — subject under test (rendering)

## Assumptions

- The Playwright approach mirrors `slot-logs.spec.js` (page route interception / injected client state); a live or stubbed proxy is available as in existing specs.
- Test-only change; no production code modified in this work item.

# Remove stale REFACTOR markers when their work item closes

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `REFACTOR-<id>` marker comments into source files to suppress duplicate work-item creation, but there is no removal path: once the referenced smell is fixed (or judged a false positive) and its work item closes, the marker persists and — because `has_existing_comment(file_path, smell_type)` matches on *smell type* only — permanently suppresses detection of that smell type in that file.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement pipeline's refactor step — they trust duplicate suppression to be accurate; a stale marker silently hides a real regression.
- **Developers reading source files** — stale markers are noise that misrepresents outstanding work.
- **Producers triaging the Refactor backlog** — a closed work item should leave no trace in the codebase.

Example user stories:

- "As an agent running the refactor step, when a marker's work item is already closed, I want the marker gone (or ignored) so I do not skip a smell that has regressed."
- "As a developer, when a refactor item is completed or judged a false positive, I want its comment removed from the file without touching surrounding code or line endings."
- "As a producer, I want a single command that reports every stale marker in the project and can clean them up."

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` provides `inject_refactor_comment()`, `has_existing_comment()`, `get_comment_style()` and `_build_comment_block()`; there is **no removal function**.
- Two slightly different regexes parse markers: `comment_injection.REFACTOR_PATTERN` (`REFACTOR-(\S+).*?smell:\s*(\S+)`, DOTALL) and `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN` (multi-line, expects a comment prefix before `smell:`).
- Markers are written in two shapes: line-prefixed (`# <!-- REFACTOR-…` … `# -->` for Python/YAML/shell, `// <!-- …` for JS/TS) and native block (`<!-- … -->` for Markdown/HTML). CSS-family files use `/* … */` with ` * ` prefixes.
- `inject_refactor_comment()` reads and writes text mode without `newline=""`, so injected files are normalised; removal must not repeat that mistake.
- `StatusLifecycle.show()` and `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()` already provide safe work-item lookup and prefix-to-sibling worklog-store resolution. Verified: a bare `wl show <foreign-prefix-id>` fails ("Work item not found"), so a sweep **must** inject `--worklog-dir` from the shared resolver.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` `remediate_pre_existing()` injects markers only for smells it just filed items for; the pipeline syncs the worklog first (`wl sync --if-idle`) and has no post-close hook.
- The canonical source of the skill is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/` (symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor`); its tests live in `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`, with `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (1251 lines) covering the current API.
- Stale markers confirmed at HEAD in the `llm` repo (work-item state checked 2026-10-20):

| File | Marker | Item stage |
|---|---|---|
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` | open / `intake_complete` — reported false positive |
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:8` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTV87EC4006EU5Z` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTRWI65I005VXOC` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR` | completed / `done` |

- The same defect is visible in the `SorraAgents` repo itself: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (2 markers), `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` (3), `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (2), `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_regressions.py` — 4 of these reference `completed` items, the rest reference `open / idea` items.

## Desired change

1. **Removal API** in `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`: `remove_refactor_marker(file_path, work_item_id) -> dict` (or a small dataclass) that locates the whole marker block for that id — line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes — and deletes it, leaving the remainder of the file byte-identical (including CRLF/LF and the file's original trailing newline). Absent marker → `{"removed": False, "reason": "absent"}`; repeated runs are no-ops.
2. **Sweep module** (new `skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py`): discover markers in repo-tracked files (exclude `.worklog/`, `node_modules`, binaries), group by referenced work-item id to one `wl show` per distinct id (worklog dir resolved via `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`), classify each marker as `stale` (stage `in_review`/`done`/`completed` or status `completed`), `active` (any other resolved stage) or `unknown` (lookup failed), and return a structured report.
3. **Trigger** from the refactor pipeline: run the sweep after the `wl sync` and **before** smell detection, so `has_existing_comment` never observes a stale marker. Non-fatal on `wl` failure (log a warning, keep markers). Standalone CLI entry point (`--sweep-markers`, report-only by default, `--apply` to delete) and a skip flag (`--no-marker-sweep`).
4. **`has_existing_comment` correctness**: keep it a pure file predicate by default, but accept an optional `is_active` resolver/callback so a caller can exclude terminal items; the pipeline's sweep-before-detect ordering is what makes the default path correct. `unknown` markers keep suppressing (conservative) and are reported as warnings.
5. **False-positive path**: a marker whose item is still open but was judged a false positive must be removable explicitly (`--remove-marker <work-item-id>` or `remove_refactor_marker()` called directly), independent of item stage.
6. **Unit tests** in `tests/test_refactor/`: removal for `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes; block and line-prefix styles; CRLF preservation; absent-marker no-op; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file touching only the target block; classification of `in_review`/`done`/`completed`/`open`; `unknown` id kept and reported; dry-run performs no writes; cross-store id resolution.
7. **Sweep the existing stale markers** in `llm` (6 stale; the false positive needs an explicit decision) and in `SorraAgents` (4 stale), so `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` afterwards shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
8. **Documentation**: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (§ REFACTOR Comments + flags table + report keys), `docs/refactor.md` (§ 4 Work Item Creation, troubleshooting "Duplicate work items created", module reference), and module docstrings. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (ship pipeline owns it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `remove_refactor_marker()` removes a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block (line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles) from a file while leaving all surrounding content byte-identical and preserving the file's line endings (verified by a CRLF fixture test).
- [ ] Removal is a no-op (`removed=False`) when the marker is absent, and re-running it is idempotent.
- [ ] A sweep reports every marker in the project with its referenced item's stage and a classification of `stale` / `active` / `unknown`; removal is triggered for markers whose work item is at a terminal stage (`in_review`, `done`, `completed`).
- [ ] Sweep work-item lookups resolve the correct worklog store via the shared resolver (a foreign-prefix id resolves; failure is non-fatal and keeps the marker as `unknown`).
- [ ] `has_existing_comment()` no longer suppresses detection for closed work items — covered by a test asserting a terminal-stage marker is not treated as an existing comment on the sweep-before-detect path (and via the optional active-item filter).
- [ ] An explicit false-positive removal path exists for markers whose work item is still open, with `--dry-run` making no writes.
- [ ] Running the sweep (apply mode) removes the 6 stale `llm` markers listed above and the 4 stale `SorraAgents` markers; a follow-up `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles; absent marker; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file; terminal vs non-terminal classification; unknown id; dry-run no-write.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Canonical source is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/`; never edit `~/.pi/agent/skills/...` (the installer replaces it) and never hand-edit markers in `llm` outside an authorised implementation run.
- Standard library only — no new third-party dependencies.
- One `wl show` per distinct referenced work-item id (cached per run); the sweep must stay in the same sub-second-to-low-seconds envelope as the existing pipeline rather than spawning per marker.
- Sweep is read-only unless `--apply` (or the default pipeline policy) removes stale markers; `--dry-run` must never write.
- Never remove a marker for an item that is not terminal unless explicitly requested by id.
- Only scan git-tracked files in the repo root (skip `.worklog/`, worktrees, `node_modules`, binary files).
- Work-item ids may belong to sibling project stores; always route `wl` through the shared resolver, not the cwd default.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — add `remove_refactor_marker()`, a single tolerant marker parser covering both existing regexes, `is_active` filter hook on `has_existing_comment()`, and `newline=""` IO.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py` (new) — marker discovery, per-id work-item lookup via `shared.status_lifecycle`, classification and report structure.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — sweep step after `wl sync` / before detection, `--sweep-markers`, `--apply`, `--remove-marker`, `--no-marker-sweep` flags, report keys.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reuse the unified marker pattern instead of its own `REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — marker lifecycle and new flags.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/docs/refactor.md` — § 4, troubleshooting, module reference.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — extend with removal tests.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_marker_sweep.py` (new) — sweep classification, dry-run, unknown ids, non-fatal wl failures.
- `llm`: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py`, `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — sweep targets only (no hand edits).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repository placement (assumption A1):** the skill's source of truth is `SorraAgents`, so the code change belongs there with its own `SA-` work item; this `LP-` item then owns the `llm` sweep. Risk: `implement.py` creates worktrees from the cwd's `.worklog`, so an `LP-` item cannot host edits under `~/projects/SorraAgents`. Needs producer confirmation (Q1).
- **No close hook:** `wl` exposes no plugin/hook on close (only `wl plugins` for discovery), so "triggered when the item reaches a terminal stage" is implemented as a sweep at refactor-run time plus a standalone command — not an event. Assumption A2.
- **False-positive regression loop:** removing the marker for a closed false-positive item re-enables detection, so the next scan re-files the same item. Mitigation: false positives must be closed with a reason *and* either fixed or excluded via `.refactor.json`/per-file ignore; the sweep should report (not silently hide) this case. Scope-creep risk — an ignore-list mechanism is a separate work item.
- **Mixed answers to `unknown`:** unresolvable ids (deleted items, wrong store) could hide real work. Conservative default: keep + warn.
- **Formatting churn:** a naive implementation strips a leading blank line or rewrites CRLF files, producing whole-file diffs. Byte-preserving IO (`newline=""`, explicit trailing-newline handling) plus a CRLF fixture test is mandatory.
- **Regex divergence:** the two existing patterns disagree on block styles; unifying them is required or Markdown/CSS markers will be missed by the sweep.
- **Scope creep:** generalising to a lifecycle framework for all agent-injected comments is out of scope; record as a separate item if it surfaces.

## Open questions

Research: all `llm` markers resolve today except none; `LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` is open at `intake_complete` while the marker is documented as a false positive. **Recommended:** keep `unknown` markers and warn; require an explicit `--remove-marker <id>` for open-item false positives.

# Retire guessed usage-limit reset for opencode accounts using /v1/usage seconds_to_reset

## Goal

Replace the *guessed* reset time used for `GoUsageLimitError` quarantine
(`provider._usage_limit_reset_info`, LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8) with the
authoritative `monthly.resetsAt` seconds available from the `/v1/usage` poll
introduced by LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P, for `opencode-*` accounts.

## Scope

- For `opencode-*` accounts with a fresh quota snapshot, use the derived
  `seconds_to_reset` from the poller instead of the rolled-dice
  `_usage_limit_guess_cap_seconds` / `_parse_resets_in` path when a
  `GoUsageLimitError` is observed.
- Keep the guessing path for non-`opencode-*` accounts (no quota source).
- Guard: if the snapshot is stale or absent, fall back to the existing guess so
  behaviour never blocks on missing quota state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A `GoUsageLimitError` on an `opencode-*` account with a fresh snapshot quarantines for exactly the snapshot's `seconds_to_reset` (+ configured margin), asserted in a test that fakes the error and a known snapshot.
- AC2 — With a stale or absent snapshot the existing guessing path is used unchanged (regression: current `test_usage_limit_reset.py` cases still pass).
- AC3 — The obsolete guessed-reset code paths for these accounts are removed or clearly marked dead, and the change is documented here. Clarification: because AC2 keeps the guess as the stale/absent fallback, "removed or marked dead" means the guessed branch is unreachable for an `opencode-*` account with a fresh snapshot; it is retained — and documented as fallback-only — for every other case. No other reset behaviour is retired.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_usage_limit_reset_info`,
  `_usage_limit_reset_seconds`, `_usage_limit_guess_cap_seconds`,
  `_parse_resets_in`, `_set_usage_limit_quarantine`, and the two 429 call sites
  (≈ lines 7277 and 8606).
- `proxy/proxy/quota_state.py` — `get_quota_snapshot`, `quota_behaviour`,
  `quota_state_max_age_seconds`, `QuotaSnapshot.seconds_to_reset`.
- `proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py` — unit + end-to-end regression tests.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — usage-limit quarantine contract (guessed-vs-explicit
  reset, margins, account key).
- `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` — quota-surge design doc reference section.

## Dependencies

- Depends on `Quota poller and derived state (tracer bullet)`
  (LP-0MVF7KEG7007C8MF) — dependency edge recorded in Worklog.
- The poller is already on `dev` (commits f7015f35, 41ef041e, 05d37fe7), so the
  previously stated "blocked on the parent epic shipping to `dev`" condition is
  satisfied on `dev`; the `dev`→`main` release is a ship-skill concern and does
  not block implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

1. **Tests first** (`proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py`), injecting a known
   snapshot via `quota_state.snapshot_from_usage` + `quota_state.set_clock` and
   resetting state in fixtures:
   - a `GoUsageLimitError` 429 on an `opencode-*` entry with a fresh snapshot →
     quarantine equals `snapshot.seconds_to_reset + 120 s`;
   - the same with a stale snapshot (older than
     `server.quota_state_max_age_seconds`) → existing guessed/explicit path;
   - the same with no snapshot at all → existing path (AC2 regression);
   - a non-`opencode-*` entry with a snapshot present → unaffected (guess or
     explicit message path).
2. Add a resolver in `proxy/provider.py` (e.g.
   `_quota_snapshot_reset_seconds(provider_cfg, config)`) that returns the
   authoritative reset or `None`, gated by `quota_state.quota_behaviour(...)`
   (kill switch / staleness) so a disabled or stale quota source never changes
   reset behaviour.
3. Thread `provider_cfg` + `config` into `_usage_limit_reset_info` (both 429
   call sites already hold both) and prefer the snapshot-derived value for
   `opencode-*` entries when it is fresh and positive; otherwise keep the
   current `_parse_resets_in` → `metadata.limitName` guess → `None` cascade
   unchanged.
4. Mark the guessed branch fallback-only in the `_usage_limit_reset_info` /
   `_usage_limit_guess_cap_seconds` docstrings and update the `Resets`/guess
   paragraphs in `proxy/docs/routing.md` (retirement note in
   `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` §References/§interaction text).
5. Keep the existing 2-minute `_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS` margin, the
   `_usage_limit_account_key` quarantine key and `explicit=True` semantics
   untouched; log the source used (snapshot vs. message vs. guess) so the
   behaviour change is observable.

## Verification / Definition of Done

- New tests fail before the change and pass after (TDD), and the full
  `proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py` file passes unchanged (AC2).
- `quota_state` remains a pure cache read on the request path (no polling, no
  blocking, never raises) — verified by the existing `quota_state` tests plus
  the new stale/absent cases.
- `wl update` stage → `in_review` with the retirement documented in this item.

## Deliverables

- Authoritative reset for opencode quarantine
- Removed/retired guessing path for these accounts
- Regression evidence

## Notes

Discovered during planning of LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P (producer decision Q3 →
option 3a: out of scope there, tracked here). discovered-from:LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan session 2026-10-20)

Plan pre-check: effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low** → below the planning
threshold, so this item was completed via the auto-complete review path
(six review stages + AC-coverage review) rather than a full decomposition.

- Q: "AC1 says *the snapshot's* `seconds_to_reset`. `QuotaSnapshot` exposes an
  account-level (monthly) value and per-window values (`rolling`, `weekly`,
  `monthly`), and a `GoUsageLimitError` may name the exhausted window via
  `metadata.limitName`. Which is authoritative for the quarantine?"
  Answer: not yet supplied by the producer. Working assumption (AC1 read
  literally): the account-level `snapshot.seconds_to_reset` (monthly window) is
  used, matching how surge and `available_times` already treat that value
  (`docs/dev/quota-surge.md` §Derivation rules). **OPEN QUESTION** (producer) —
  matters because a weekly-limit 429 would quarantine for the monthly reset
  (up to ~30 days) instead of the weekly reset (≤7 days), a materially longer
  block.
- Q: "AC1 says *+ configured margin*. Today the margin is the module constant
  `_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS = 120` (not configurable). Is a new config
  key in scope?"
  Answer: not yet supplied. Working assumption: reuse the existing 2-minute
  constant (no new config key, no config-docs change). **OPEN QUESTION**
  (producer) — if a configurable margin is intended, this item grows to include
  `proxy/proxy/quota_state.py`-style key handling and the configuration-keys
  docs.
- Q: "When the gateway message *does* carry an explicit `Resets in ...`
  duration, does the snapshot still win for `opencode-*` accounts?"
  Answer: not yet supplied. Working assumption: yes — the snapshot wins for a
  fresh snapshot (AC1 says "exactly the snapshot's `seconds_to_reset`"), and the
  message/guess cascade remains for non-`opencode-*` entries and stale/absent
  snapshots. **OPEN QUESTION** (producer) — the alternative (explicit message
  wins over the snapshot) is defensible since both are authoritative; the
  choice changes AC1's expected value.

# Intake brief: make local GPU utilisation/prefill metrics visible to the usage report

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy usage report to measure **local prefill time**
(dispatch → first byte) alongside decode time, so "GPU busy %" reflects real slot
occupancy and large local prompts stop being invisible.

## Problem statement

`report.md` currently reports `Local model utilization → Busy time = 7h 02m (29.3%)`
and `Total compute (slot-time) = 7h 47m`, derived by pairing **local `Stream
started` → `Stream finished`**. That window starts at *first byte*, so the entire
prefill/prompt-processing phase is excluded.

For large local prompts, prefill is the dominant cost. In the same 24h window
(2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23) the proxy logged `dispatch_first_byte_ms` for
every one of the **463** local requests:

| Prefill (dispatch → first byte) | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Samples | 463 |
| p10 | 3.3 s |
| **median** | **61.8 s** |
| p90 | 269.8 s |
| max | 817 s (13.6 min) |
| **Sum** | **14.3 h** |

Examples: `dispatch_first_byte_ms=98697.8 cache_state=warm cached_ratio=0.942` and
`dispatch_first_byte_ms=133126.9 cache_state=cold cached_ratio=0.000` (212 cold /
251 warm in the window). Adding 14.3 h of prefill to 7 h 47 m of decode puts real
occupancy near **79,500 s ≈ 46% of 48 slot-hours**, versus the 16% the report
implies. This directly misleads capacity work (slot count, ctx size, queue
tuning) — including the concurrent slot-count investigation.

Corroborating gaps in the same report:

- `## Decode speed` and `## Prompt eval speed` are **empty** ("No llama-server eval
  timing samples in window"), so there is no independent decode/prefill evidence.
  `llama-server.log*` in the window contains no `eval time` lines (older rotated
  files do, e.g. `llama-server.log-2026-10-07.gz` has 296) — ingestion or build
  verbosity likely regressed, and that must be established.
- The report's TTFT table is dominated by remote samples; local `ttft_seconds` is
  never logged (only `dispatch_first_byte_ms`).
- The prefill phase is observable in the proxy already: 11,050
  `lease_extended_during_prefill` events with `progress=None`, i.e. prefill polling
  works but exposes no numeric progress.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `proxy-usage-analysis` computes and reports **local prefill time** per local
   stream from `dispatch_first_byte_ms` (falling back to the pairing of dispatch
   and first byte when absent), including p10/p50/p90/max and the **window total**,
   with an explicit statement that the figure is slot-time, not wall-clock.
2. `Local model utilization` reports `busy` as the union of
   **dispatch → finish** intervals (prefill + decode), with the decode-only figure
   retained alongside as a separate row, and a labelled lower/upper bound. Existing
   fast/cheap bucketing and concurrency stats keep working on the new intervals.
3. A `Prefill vs decode` breakdown appears in the report (slot-seconds and % of
   slot-time each), so capacity decisions can see where slot time goes.
4. The empty decode/prompt-eval sections are fixed or explained automatically:
   determine why no llama-server eval-timing samples exist in the current window
   (`llama-server.log` verbosity / build / rotation) and either restore ingestion
   or have the report print a named, self-diagnosing reason (log path, files
   scanned, lines matched) instead of an unattributed blank.
5. Unit tests cover: the prefill parser, the union-interval busy calculation
   (including boundary-crossing and unfinished streams), the fast/cheap split on
   the new intervals, and the empty-eval-timing diagnostic path. Fixtures are
   copied from real `/var/log/llama-proxy` lines (`dispatch_first_byte_ms=`).
6. A regenerated report for the same window shows the corrected busy figure and
   the new prefill/decode split, with the numbers in this brief used as the
   expected-order sanity check (≈14.3 h prefill, ≈7.8 h decode).

## Risks / notes

- `dispatch_first_byte_ms` is logged per local request but is **not** identical to
  `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` (queue wait is split out as `queue_wait_ms`); define
  which interval maps to slot occupancy and document it.
- Unfinished/aborted local streams (2 in the window) have no `dispatch_first_byte_ms`;
  they must be reported as "unknown prefill" rather than silently dropped.
- Changing "busy" semantics changes historical comparability; keep the old
  decode-only number visible and state the definition change in the report header.
data.title: Make local GPU busy/prefill metrics visible in the proxy usage report

# Spike: quantify llama-server slot save/restore cost as the basis for "virtual slots"

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want measured numbers for KV-cache slot save/restore cost and
restore hit-rate, so we can decide whether "virtual slots" (e.g. 8 proxy-side session
slots multiplexed onto 2 physical GPU slots) is worth building, rather than guessing.

## Context / hypothesis to test

The proxy currently gates local dispatch with **2 dispatch leases**
(`session_slot_pool_size: 2`) and persists per-session KV snapshots
(`session_slot_save_path` / `LLAMA_SLOT_SAVE_PATH`, `_restore_slot_snapshot`,
`slot_save`). In the 24h window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23 there were
**2,641** `local_dispatch_denied` events (2,633 with both slots held), 5,805
contention-queue waits and 4,947 queue abandonments, while real slot occupancy was
only ≈46% once prefill (14.3 h) is added to decode (7h47m).

Hypothesis: keeping more *session* slots than *GPU* slots, and swapping a session's
KV snapshot in on demand, would let more sessions "own" local capacity without
growing the physical pool. Open question: does a restore actually avoid re-prefill
(the win), or does llama.cpp invalidate/refuse the restored cache and re-prefill
anyway (the cost)? Note: this build is Qwen3.x hybrid-attention, where llama.cpp
already invalidates its own context checkpoints, so the answer is not obvious.

## Measurements required

Using the existing harness conventions (see
`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md` for fidelity caveats):

1. **Save cost** — wall time and on-disk size of `slot save` for prompt sizes
   38K / 72K / 100K / 124K tokens; success rate (the window already shows 5
   `slot_save failed` ReadTimeouts).
2. **Restore cost + hit rate** — for a restored snapshot: `dispatch_first_byte_ms`
   vs the same session re-prefilling cold. A "hit" is a restore whose first-byte
   latency is materially below the cold prefill baseline (window baseline: median
   `dispatch_first_byte_ms` **61.8 s**, p90 **269.8 s**, max **817 s**).
3. **Invalidation behaviour** — how often the restored cache is rejected (look for
   full re-prefill / `forcing full prompt re-processing`), and the tokens re-processed.
4. **Memory/bandwidth pressure** — KV snapshot footprint per session, host page-cache
   growth for N=8 snapshots, and system MemAvailable delta.
5. **End-to-end effect under contention** — with 8 virtual slots over 2 physical
   slots and a synthetic 8-concurrent-session workload: queue abandonments,
   local serve share, and p50/p90 latency vs the N=2 baseline.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A reproducible benchmark script (committed under `proxy/benchmarks/`) that produces
   the numbers above, with fixtures/driver documented.
2. A results table in `docs/` covering save size/time, restore time, restore hit-rate,
   invalidated-restore rate, memory delta, and end-to-end contention metrics.
3. An explicit go/no-go recommendation with the break-even condition stated
   (e.g. "virtual slots pay off only if restore hit-rate ≥ X% and restore adds
   < Y s, because the cold prefill median is 61.8 s"), or a "not viable" verdict with
   the measured reason.
4. If the verdict is "not viable", name the cheaper substitutes to pursue instead
   (more physical slots — LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8; idle-aware admission; shorter
   post-stream lease), with the measured evidence for each.
5. No production behaviour change is included in this item.

## Risks / notes

- Slot save/restore has failed intermittently (ReadTimeout) — the benchmark must
  record failures rather than retry them away.
- Local decode share has been hard to isolate in previous sweeps because live agent
  sessions hold the dispatch leases; the run must hold the mode lock or record the
  same validity caveat explicitly.
- Scope boundary: this spike measures feasibility and cost only; the design and
  implementation of virtual slots (if viable) is a separate follow-up item.
data.title: Spike: quantify llama-server slot save/restore cost for virtual slots

# Intake brief: serialise local prefills so one prefill at a time gets the full GPU

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want at most one local **prefill** to run at a time (while other
slots may keep decoding), so each request's prefill gets full GPU throughput instead
of sharing it — cutting time-to-first-byte roughly in half with no loss of aggregate
throughput.

## Evidence (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23, 460 paired local dispatches)

Prefill intervals (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`, reconstructed as `[t − dur, t]`) bucketed
by how many other local prefills overlapped them:

| Overlapping prefills | n | first-byte p50 | throughput (new tok/s, p50) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 190 | **23.4 s** | **253.8** |
| 1 | 220 | 85.0 s | 156.6 |
| 2 | 48 | 119.7 s | 128.8 |
| 3 | 2 | 222.2 s | 30.9 |

- **47.8% of local prefills (220/460) shared the GPU with at least one other**
  prefill; 50 shared it with two or more.
- Aggregate throughput is **flat** (≈254 → ≈258 tok/s) while per-request throughput
  halves — i.e. concurrency adds latency, not capacity.
- Observed total prefill wall time 50,645 s vs 21,600 s if every request had run at
  the solitary 254 tok/s → **2.3× inflation** from contention plus coded-context read
  cost.

## Proposed change

Add an admission semaphore for the **prefill phase only**:

1. Track per-slot phase from the existing `/slots` poll (`is_processing`,
   `n_past`/`n_prompt_tokens_processed`, coalesced per `SLOTS_POLL_TTL_SECONDS`).
2. Allow at most `server.local_max_concurrent_prefills` (default **1**) requests in
   prefill across the pool; a request whose slot would start a second concurrent
   prefill waits (bounded) or falls back per policy.
3. A slot already decoding does not block another slot's prefill — only
   prefill-vs-prefill is serialised, so decode keeps running in parallel.
4. Emit `prefill_gate_wait_ms` per request and expose the queue depth on
   `/llama/local/status`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New config knob `server.local_max_concurrent_prefills` (default 1, 0 disables),
   documented, with validation.
2. Unit tests for the gate: second concurrent prefill waits; a decoding slot does not
   block; a request that cannot be admitted within its budget falls back exactly as
   today; disable → current behaviour.
3. Measured effect over ≥24h via `proxy-usage-analysis`: local `dispatch_first_byte_ms`
   p50/p90 (baseline p50 **61.8 s**, p90 **269.8 s**), share of prefills with ≥1
   overlap (baseline 47.8%), local serve share (baseline 2.6%), decode throughput
   (must not regress), and aggregate prefill tokens/s (must not regress).
4. No increase in `downloaded`/queue abandonment (`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`,
   baseline 4,947) — the gate must not simply move the wait elsewhere.
5. Interaction recorded with the lease system: the gate must never hold a slot while
   the pool is otherwise idle (test covers "single request alone → no added delay").

## Risks / notes

- With 2 slots, serialising prefills means one slot may idle during a long prefill
  while the other decodes; that is the intended trade (throughput is flat anyway).
- Must not starve large prefills: a 7-minute prefill blocks the gate for 7 minutes;
  combine with a prefill-ETA-aware queue (see the admission-guard item) so queued
  requests with no chance of admission fall back immediately.
- Do not confuse this gate with the existing dispatch lease (session-scoped) or the
  contention queue (slot-scoped) — this one is phase-scoped.
data.title: Serialise local prefills so one prefill at a time gets the full GPU

# Intake brief: publish truthful local capacity on `/llama/local/status` (slot phase + prefill ETA)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator (and as the ContextHub/herdr dispatcher), I want the proxy's status
endpoint to distinguish *generating*, *idle-but-leased*, and *free* slots and to
publish a prefill ETA, so dispatch decisions stop treating a reserved-but-idle GPU as
busy and stop launching sessions that will immediately queue and fall back.

## Evidence (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23)

- `local_dispatch_denied` **2,641** (2,633 with `active=2` lease records), yet local
  was decoding only 29.3% of wall clock, and the 04:00–05:00 hour logged **187**
  denials at 2.5% local busy.
- `proxy/config.yaml` already records the same finding from an earlier analysis:
  "Log analysis (5.3h, 198 local_dispatch_denied events) showed **100% of denies
  caused by idle lease holders, never GPU saturation**".
- The dispatcher (`ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) already prefers
  per-slot detail (`slots[].is_processing`, `owner_session_id`) over the untrusted
  `available_slots` count, and reads `contention_queue_depth` — but a slot held by an
  *inactive* lease is indistinguishable from a working one, and there is no ETA.
- Prefill dominates the hold time (p50 61.8 s, p90 269.8 s), so "busy" without an ETA
  is not actionable for a dispatcher that must decide *before* spawning an agent.

## Proposed change

Extend the local status payload (additive, backward compatible — older consumers keep
working):

```json
{
  "slots": [
    {"slot_id": "0", "is_processing": true, "phase": "prefill|decode",
     "owner_session_id": "…", "lease_state": "generating|idle_leased|free",
     "context_tokens": 102345, "prefill_eta_seconds": 187.0}
  ],
  "total_slots": 2, "available_slots": 0,
  "contention_queue_depth": 3, "queue_eta_seconds": 240.0,
  "prefill_budget_seconds": 120,
  "capacity_hint": "saturated|prefill_bound|idle"
}
```

Rules: `lease_state` distinguishes an idle lease from active work; `prefill_eta_seconds`
is derived from the same calibration used by the admission guard; `capacity_hint`
summarises whether the pool is genuinely working.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New fields are additive and versioned; a client that ignores them behaves exactly
   as today (contract test with an old-shaped consumer).
2. `lease_state` is correct in all three cases, including a session holding an inactive
   lease after its stream finished (test), and never reports `free` while a prefill or
   decode is in flight.
3. `prefill_eta_seconds` / `queue_eta_seconds` come from the shared calibration (one
   source of truth with the admission guard), and are `null` when not computable rather
   than a misleading 0.
4. `capacity_hint` is documented with its exact decision table and unit-tested
   (saturated / prefill_bound / idle).
5. Documented consumer contract in `proxy/docs/` (and a pointer from
   `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`'s parser notes) so the dispatcher
   can gate on `lease_state` and `prefill_eta_seconds`.
6. Correlated measurement: while the fields are live, record denials-per-hour and
   local busy to confirm the signal matches reality (baseline: 187 denials in a
   2.5%-busy hour).

## Risks / notes

- Status polling must not add load: reuse the existing `/slots` coalescing
  (`SLOTS_POLL_TTL_SECONDS`, single-flight).
- Do not expose stale data as fresh: keep `slots_stale` semantics and mark ETA `null`
  when the underlying `/slots` poll is stale.
- The consumer change (herdr gating on the new fields) lives in ContextHub and is a
  separate item there; this item only guarantees the contract.
data.title: Publish truthful local capacity on /llama/local/status (slot phase + prefill ETA)

# Intake brief: re-widen local size gates only once cache warmth is proven (capacity-gated)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I still want large prompts (38K–124K tokens) served locally **when the
GPU can actually absorb them** — but only after cache-warmth work has cut the cost per
request, and with admission sized to measured capacity rather than to a fixed token
threshold.

## Why this replaces the two deleted widening items

The previously filed items — "warm threshold to 95% of per-slot context"
(LP-0MVGCOZMZ003I6PF, deleted) and "economic bypass for medium priority"
(LP-0MVGD9YLM0055SFF, deleted) — were deleted because, as scoped, they widen admission
faster than the GPU can absorb, which makes cache churn and first-token latency worse:

| Band | Requests / 24h | Median prompt | Cold cost at 254 new tok/s | Slot-hours needed | Prefill headroom available |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100,000–124,518 (`context_too_large`) | 890 | ~110k | ~430 s each | **~107 h** | ~26 h |
| 38,000–100,000 (`large_context_bypass`) | 1,284 | ~71k | ~280 s each | **~100 h** | ~26 h |

Headroom = 48 slot-hours/day − 28,020 s decode − 50,645 s measured prefill ≈ 26 h
(≈23.8 M new tokens at 254 tok/s). Both bands are ~4× over capacity **cold**, and ≈10
slot-hours each at a 90% cache-hit rate — i.e. they fit *only* with warm caches.

## Preconditions (blocking)

1. **Cache warmth**: `cached_ratio` seeded from persisted slot snapshots
   (LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) — measured by the share of local dispatches that are
   `cache_state=cold` (baseline **45.7%**, 210/460).
2. **Admission control**: prefill-ETA-aware admission guard (the "stop starting local
   work that cannot finish in budget" item) so a widened gate cannot turn into
   queue-then-fallback stalls.
3. **Prefill protection**: prefill serialisation so widened admission does not halve
   per-request prefill throughput via contention (baseline: 47.8% of prefills shared the
   GPU, p50 85 s with one overlap vs 23.4 s alone).

## Proposed change (only after the preconditions land)

Replace the two fixed token thresholds' *effective* behaviour with a **capacity-aware
admission** rule layered on the existing thresholds:

- Keep `context_too_large` as the hard physical cap (`ctx // slots − 4096` = 126,976).
- For the economic band, admit locally while the projected slot-hours of admitted
  traffic stay within a configured share of idle capacity (e.g.
  `local_capacity_admission_budget_ratio: 0.8` of measured idle slot-time), and fall
  back to remote when the projection exceeds it.
- Raise the warm threshold toward 95% of per-slot (124,518 at N=2) **only** as the
  measured cache-hit rate supports it; report the achieved setting.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Preconditions evidenced in comments before implementation starts: cold-dispatch
   share materially below 45.7%, admission guard live, prefill serialisation live.
2. The admission rule is capacity-based, not threshold-only: a projection exceeding the
   configured idle-slot budget routes remote early, and the projection is recomputed from
   rolling observed data (no fixed constant).
3. Measured over ≥24h after enabling: local serve share rises from 2.6%; `cache_state=cold`
   share does **not** rise above the 45.7% baseline; `dispatch_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 do
   **not** regress beyond a stated budget (baseline 61.8 s / 269.8 s); queue abandonment
   does **not** exceed the 4,947 baseline; `finish_reason=length` stays at zero.
4. A rollback switch (`local_capacity_admission_enabled`) with a documented revert path.
5. The achieved warm threshold and the reason for it (measured hit-rate) are recorded in
   the config comment and in the item.

## Risks / notes

- This is deliberately a *follow-on* item: implementing it first reproduces the harm the
  deleted items would have caused.
- Compaction is the complementary lever (reduces `est_tokens` rather than cost/token);
  the compaction dry-run currently reports 110/347 sessions that would have triggered —
  that is the potential supply-side reduction to weigh against local admission.
